completion_data.completion_summary: Phase 8's decision gate landed its verdict as a compiled object: FAIL, on sub-question (i), ADMISSIBILITY. The schema IdleGapLengthening is stated as a named def in the new standalone prototype specs/838_two_sided_open_core_pin_free_pigeonhole/prototype/idle-gap-lengthening.lean (299 lines, namespace Probe838C) and refuted there by idleGapLengthening_refuted on the standard axiom profile with no sorryAx. The obstruction is not pinCompat_of_ladderPath, which does loosen as the plan argued, but step itself: an idle run of length two requires an idle-to-idle edge in the object's step graph, which an object satisfying ParamsOk need not have, so the idle run's length is a datum of the object rather than a parameter the construction may raise. no_consecutive_idle_of_no_idle_step is the generic reading and the two-state object Qo := Bool with stepO x y = x || y is the witness. Sub-question (ii), type preservation, was never reached and is recorded as untouched. No library file changed; the reserved name cellLE_zero_const_of_kappa_eq remains claimed by nothing. Phase 9 proceeds on its FAIL branch.

memory_candidates.title: A decision gate about inserting positions into a ladder path can fail at the step graph, below the pin condition
memory_candidates.content: When a construction over ladder paths proposes to lengthen an idle run, the pin-compatibility condition is the wrong place to look for the obstruction: it loosens as a region start moves farther away. The binding constraint is one level below, in step itself -- an idle run of length two requires an idle-to-idle edge in the object's step graph, and nothing in ParamsOk supplies one. Before designing the pin arithmetic for such a construction, check whether the object's step graph admits the run length at all; a two-state object with that single edge removed refutes the whole schema in four lines.

memory_candidates.title: Reusing a permissive prototype object can make a refutation impossible to state
memory_candidates.content: Sibling prototypes in this repository use step = fun _ _ => true, which admits every walk. That object cannot carry any refutation whose mechanism is a missing edge: it has none. When a gate's expected failure mode is an object-level restriction, declare a fresh minimal object rather than reusing the permissive one, and say in the record why the reuse was impossible.
